sections.title: 🎯 What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Let’s make your code cleaner and faster with Augmented Assignment Operators! These are like shortcuts for common math operations.

• What augmented assignment operators are (+=, -=, *=, etc.)
• How they make your code shorter and clearer
• When to use them (and when not to!)

sections.title: 💡 Concept Explanation
sections.content:
Imagine you’re at a lemonade stand. Instead of saying ‘I’ll take my current number of lemons and add 5 more,’ you just say ‘add 5 lemons.’ That’s exactly what augmented assignment operators do!

They combine an operation (like addition) with assignment in one step. For example:
• Instead of `x = x + 2`, you write `x += 2`
• Instead of `total = total * 1.1`, you write `total *= 1.1`

These operators work with all basic math operations:
• `+=` (addition)
• `-=` (subtraction)
• `*=` (multiplication)
• `/=` (division)
• `%=` (remainder)

sections.title: 📊 Visual Simulation
sections.content: Step-by-step visualization of how Augmented Assignment Operators works:

steps.title: Before Augmented Assignment
steps.description: Traditional way: You write the variable twice
steps.code:
int score = 10;
score = score + 5;  // score becomes 15

steps.title: With Augmented Assignment
steps.description: Cleaner way: Variable appears only once
steps.code:
int score = 10;
score += 5;  // Same result, less typing!

steps.title: Order Matters!
steps.description: Expressions are evaluated right-to-left. Parentheses come first!

sections.title: ⚡ Key Points
points: ✓ Augmented operators combine math and assignment in one step
✓ They make code shorter and often more readable
✓ Work with all basic math operations (+, -, *, /, %)
✓ Right side is evaluated first (like regular math)

sections.title: 🔥 Tips & Mistakes
dos: Use them for simple math updates (e.g., counters, totals)
Keep expressions simple to avoid confusion
donts: Don’t use with complex expressions (hard to read!)
Avoid mixing with other operators without parentheses
sections.protip: Use `+=` for string concatenation too! `message += "!";` adds an exclamation mark.

sections.title: 🌍 Real World Use
sections.content: Where is Augmented Assignment Operators used in real apps?

examples.how: Quickly update player scores: `playerScore += 10;` when they collect coins
Calculate totals with tax: `total *= 1.08;` to add 8% tax
Increment likes: `likeCount += 1;` when users click the heart button

problem.description:
Fix this code to use augmented assignment operators. The program should calculate:
1. A 10% tip on a $50 bill
2. The remaining balance after spending $20 from $100
hints: Replace `bill = bill + tip` with an augmented operator
problem.explanation: We replaced `bill = bill + tip` with `bill += tip` and `wallet = wallet - 20` with `wallet -= 20`. The results are identical but the code is cleaner!

sections.title: 📝 Summary
points: 📌 Augmented operators = math + assignment in one step
📌 Most important rule: Right side evaluates first!
📌 Practice with counters, totals, and simple updates
📌 Ready for next topic: Increment/Decrement Operators (++, --)!
